key_insight: This review traces how materials literature mining has evolved from rule-based pipelines to LLMs and agentic systems that extract information from text, tables, and figures.
engineering_relevance: Automated extraction can populate materials databases and knowledge graphs, support research assistants, and enable closed-loop discovery when integrated with autonomous laboratories.
method: Review rule-based, NLP, transformer-encoder, and LLM-based extraction approaches.
Assess generated datasets, extraction accuracy, computational costs, and methodological trade-offs.
Outline practical guidelines for reliable, scalable materials data extraction.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a review of datasets and evaluation practices, but reports no quantitative results and highlights a shortage of reliable benchmarks.
watch_item: Reliable sample-level linking of structure, properties, processing, and performance remains challenging, especially with non-standard terminology across document modalities.
paper_title: Automated Materials Data and Knowledge Extraction using Machine Learning and Large Language Models
